step1.programTitle: Diploma in Logistics and Supply Chain Management
step1.entryRequirements:
Academic prerequisites:
- Higher Secondary Certificate (10+2) or equivalent; or a recognised Level 3 qualification (e.g., A-Levels or equivalent). Applicants should demonstrate passes in English and Mathematics (or Commerce/Accounts) or their regional equivalents. A minimum overall score of 50% (or grade C) is normally expected.
- Applicants holding a prior diploma or degree in any discipline are welcome and may receive recognition of prior learning where appropriate.

Professional experience:
- Not required for entry. However, applicants with 6–24 months of relevant experience (e.g., warehousing, transport operations, retail distribution, freight forwarding) are encouraged to apply and may be considered for RPL/APEL where evidence of competence is demonstrated.

Other requirements:
- English language proficiency: CEFR B2 (e.g., IELTS 5.5 with no band below 5.0) or equivalent. Applicants educated in English-medium schools or holding equivalent qualifications may be exempt.
- Digital literacy: basic proficiency with office productivity tools, especially spreadsheets (sorting, filtering, basic formulas); ability to use email, online collaboration tools and web-based platforms.
- Minimum age 18 at the point of enrolment. A personal statement may be requested to establish motivation and fit for the programme.

Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL/APEL):
- Prior certificated learning and/or experiential learning will be considered in line with institutional policy and AGI Academic Standards. Evidence may include transcripts, employer attestations, work products and supervisor references.
- Up to 50% of the programme (maximum 30 UK credits, equivalent to 300 learning hours) may be awarded via RPL/APEL, provided learning outcomes are fully met and currency can be demonstrated.

modules.title: Supply Chain and Logistics Fundamentals for Kerala Industries
topics: Kerala supply chain landscape and Kochi port overview
SCOR processes: Plan, Source, Make, Deliver, Return, Enable
Stakeholders and roles: shippers, 3PLs, customs brokers and carriers
Compliance basics: GST, e-way bills, HS codes and ICEGATE
Digital foundations: WMS, TMS, ERP and GS1 basics
Sustainability and reverse logistics essentials
Warehouse and transport safety culture; ethics and data confidentiality
Kerala case studies: retail, e-commerce and manufacturing

modules.title: Quantitative Methods and Data Analytics for Supply Chains
topics: Descriptive statistics and visualisation for logistics
Data quality, cleansing and validation
Demand analysis basics: moving averages and simple smoothing
EOQ, safety stock and reorder point calculations
Cycle counting and variance analysis
Spreadsheet modelling in Excel/Google Sheets
Operational dashboards and KPI reporting
Shipment tracking metrics: lead time and on-time delivery

modules.title: Warehouse Operations, WMS and GS1 Barcoding
topics: Receiving, put-away and location control

Picking methods, packing and dispatch
